sections.heading: Why a Properly Functioning Door Closer Matters for Your Reston Property
sections.body: A door closer does far more than simply pull a door shut. It controls the speed and force of closure, protects the door frame from impact damage, and helps maintain interior climate conditions. In high-traffic commercial environments — from the busy office towers near Reston Town Center to the retail corridors along Sunset Hills Road — a malfunctioning door closer can accelerate wear on the door, the frame, and adjacent glass panels. Over time, a door that slams or fails to latch properly can compromise the overall security of your building. Property managers who address door closer issues quickly avoid the cascading repair costs that come from neglected hardware. Our technicians assess the full closer system, including the arm, bracket, and body, to identify the root cause rather than offering a temporary fix.

sections.heading: Common Door Closer Problems We Repair in Reston
sections.body: Door closers can fail in several distinct ways, and recognizing the signs early helps you schedule service before a minor issue becomes a major one. The most common problems we encounter at Reston commercial properties include closers that no longer control door speed, resulting in doors that slam shut or swing too slowly to latch. Hydraulic fluid leaks are another frequent issue — once the fluid seal breaks down, the closer loses its dampening function entirely. We also regularly repair bent or broken closer arms, stripped adjustment screws, and mounting hardware that has worked loose from the door or frame over time. In older commercial buildings near areas like Lake Anne Village Center, we often find door closers that are simply past their service life and need full replacement. Whether your closer needs adjustment, component repair, or full replacement, we carry the parts and expertise to handle it on-site.

sections.heading: Our Commercial Door Closer Repair Process
sections.body: We keep our repair process straightforward so your business experiences as little disruption as possible. When you call us, we gather basic information about your door closer system and the symptoms you are experiencing, allowing our technician to arrive prepared with the appropriate tools and replacement parts. On-site, we begin with a thorough inspection of the closer body, arm assembly, spring tension, and mounting points. We check closing speed, latching speed, and backcheck function — the built-in resistance that prevents a door from swinging open too forcefully. Based on our findings, we walk you through the recommended repair approach before beginning any work. Our team services all major commercial door closer brands and models, and we work efficiently to get your entrance back in proper operation the same day in most cases.

sections.heading: When to Replace Rather Than Repair a Commercial Door Closer
sections.body: Not every door closer problem warrants a repair — in some situations, full replacement is the more practical and cost-effective solution. If a closer body is physically damaged, has a cracked housing, or has experienced a complete hydraulic failure, attempting to repair it may only delay an inevitable replacement. Similarly, older closers that no longer have available replacement parts are strong candidates for a new unit. When we assess a door closer at a Reston property and determine that replacement is the better path, we help you select an appropriate unit based on the door's weight, width, and traffic volume. We install the new closer, adjust all settings for proper function, and verify that the door operates correctly before we leave. Our goal is always to give you an honest assessment so you can make the right decision for your property and budget.
